page: Microsoft Azure D48ps_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the arm64 architecture utilizing Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 processors clocked at 3.4 GHz. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 48 dedicated physical cores with single-thread execution per core, eliminating hyperthreading contention. The CPU configuration includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a centralized 128 MB L3 cache array. It is paired with 192.0 GB of RAM, preserving a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local storage, nor does it feature dedicated GPU hardware or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel compute and memory subsystems. In multi-threaded testing, the instance achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 21743.0 and a stress-ng multi-core result of 99388.23. The memory subsystem ranks in the top tier across uncached testing, reaching 464.92 GB/sec in large-block read operations and 173.04 GB/sec in write operations, alongside a PassMark memory score of 3362.4. In-memory data processing is further validated by a PassMark database score of 37101.66 and 89.47 million operations per second during Redis SET testing. Static web serving throughput reaches 72.54 GB/sec, while software compilation via Clang produces a strong score of 56873.0.

Single-threaded execution represents a clear tradeoff, with stress-ng single-core performance at 2074.99 and Geekbench single-core score at 1649.0 placing in the middle quartile. Because local storage is absent, persistent data operations rely on network-attached storage. Hardware acceleration is absent, and small-model LLM generation shows lower relative throughput, although medium-model generation reaches 31.48 tokens per second. The server offers strong qualitative cost efficiency for scaled infrastructures where memory bandwidth and dedicated core counts matter more than peak single-thread frequency. Primary recommended workloads include high-throughput Redis caching, database clusters, distributed build nodes, and concurrent web serving.
description: Microsoft Azure D48ps_v6 is a general purpose instance powered by an ARM Neoverse-N2 processor running at 3.4 GHz. It features 48 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, 128 MB of L3 cache, and 192 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio. The instance delivers high memory throughput, achieving 464.92 GB/sec in large-block uncached read benchmarks and 173.04 GB/sec in write benchmarks. Multi-threaded compute performance is strong, indicated by a Geekbench multi-core score of 21743.0 and strong results in Clang software compilation and Redis operations. The platform contains no integrated local NVMe storage and lacks hardware GPU acceleration, requiring reliance on remote storage options for persistent disk I/O. Given its execution density and high memory bandwidth, the D48ps_v6 provides reliable cost efficiency for multi-threaded backend services, high-concurrency web serving, CI/CD compilation pipelines, and in-memory caching layers.
